record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Periodic orbit existence in symplectic billiards
record.original_question: Does every polygon admit at least one periodic orbit for the symplectic billiard dynamics?

evidence.quote: Question 2: Does every polygon have a periodic orbit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Symplectic billiards are defined as follows. Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a convex polygon with boundary $\partial P$, oriented counterclockwise. The symplectic billiard map $T$ acts on ordered pairs of points $(x,y)\in\partial P\times\partial P$ as follows: given $(x,y)$, the image $T(x,y)=(y,z)$ is determined by the rule that the tangent line to $\partial P$ at $y$ is parallel to the chord $xz$ (equivalently, $z$ is the unique boundary point such that $z-x$ is parallel to the side of $\partial P$ containing $y$, with the appropriate orientation). At vertices, the dynamics is extended in the natural way using the cone of admissible tangent directions. A periodic orbit of period $n$ is a sequence of boundary points $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ with $T(x_i,x_{i+1})=(x_{i+1},x_{i+2})$ for all $i$ (indices modulo $n$).

Question: Does every convex polygon $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ admit at least one periodic orbit of the symplectic billiard map?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (e.g., the 2024 work on symplectic billiards for pairs of polygons and the open-problems compendium from 2026) state that it is unknown whether every convex polygon carries a periodic symplectic billiard orbit, paralleling the analogous open question for ordinary polygonal billiards. For pairs of polygons, an example with no periodic orbit has recently been constructed, but for a single polygon the existence question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic billiards for pairs of polygons
status_evidence.snippet: It is unknown whether every convex polygon carries a periodic symplectic billiard orbit (this question is also open for the usual polygonal billiards).
status_evidence.claim: The existence of periodic orbits for the symplectic billiard map in every convex polygon is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Polygonal symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectic billiards in affine-regular polygons and trapezoids are fully periodic; existence of periodic orbits in general polygons is not established.
status_evidence.claim: General existence of periodic orbits in arbitrary convex polygons is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Listed open problem: does every polygon admit a periodic symplectic billiard orbit?
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in a recent open-problems survey.
